## Repository findings

There is **no existing app or game implementation** in the repository: no HTML entry page, JavaScript/TypeScript source, package manifest, framework configuration, game code, or app-specific art/assets. The tracked project files are only the README and OpenCode workflow; the remaining root files are untracked setup scripts/instructions.

### Relevant files

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/README.md` — project boilerplate; contains no app or implementation guidance.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/Agents.md` — repository conventions. In particular, its “Mobile browser games” section requires responsive layouts, usable touch controls, safe-area awareness, and avoiding browser gesture conflicts.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh` — invokes the external runtime’s `scripts/default-start.mjs`; it expects `RUNTIME_DIR` to be set. This is a wrapper, not a project-level `npm start` script.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/capture.sh` — invokes the external runtime’s capture script.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/startup.sh` — currently only enables strict shell options; it has no app startup logic.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/.gitignore` — excludes generated/runtime directories and `node_modules`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/.github/workflows/opencode.yml` — automation workflow; not a game entry point.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/.agents/README.md` — describes bundled agent skills. The files under `.agents/skills/` are tooling, not game code or app assets.

## What to add for a playable game

Create the app entry point and implementation from scratch—for example, an `index.html` plus JavaScript/CSS files, or a framework setup with a package manifest and documented run command. Add original or otherwise appropriately licensed monster and environment art; there are no app-specific assets to build on.

For the game itself, implement a complete playable loop: explore a small world, encounter monsters, capture them, and show collection/progress. Include touch-first movement and interaction controls, with layouts that fit phone screens and safe areas. Keep gameplay usable without relying on motion controls. No files were edited.
</subagent>

## Mosslight — Little Wilds

A cozy, touch-first monster-catching game that runs directly in a browser. Open `index.html` or serve this folder with any static web server.

- Wander the meadow with the on-screen directional pad or **WASD / arrow keys**.
- Approach a wild spirit and use **Soften** to improve your chances before offering an orb.
- Track your discoveries in the field journal. Collection progress and remaining orbs save in your browser.
